R2.summary: plan_tool.py record-judges BLOCK FILE --sha256 H. FILE exactly {kind: 'stage1 judge completion record', block, judges: {harmbench: {tag, result_sha256, run_record_sha256, bundle_sha256, exit, judged, complete}, granite: {+known_answer_passed}}, index_sha256, utc, recorded_by}; one or both judges; any other key refuses (so no HB/Granite/yes/unparsed/harm count can be recorded). Record time: each judge has a released judge launch and no not-run decision; exit 0, complete true, Granite gate passed; the launch's own tmp/judge-pod/TAG/judge-pod-result.json hashes to result_sha256 and agrees (kind, tag, judge, bundle, exit, complete, judged, fetched run record SHA-256, confirmed stop, gate) and its fetched run record hashes to run_record_sha256, and its verified units include every required unit (read by key, never printed: an addition to R2, so the record is not typed). Record time and every later use: FILE re-hashed (and its block/judges/index_sha256 equal to plan.json's copy), judges/BLOCK/judge-files-index.json at index_sha256, a sealed block's seal (re-hashed) holds that index with that SHA-256, and R3's check. One record per block; adds plan.json records.judges[BLOCK] and an operator-actions line; changes no seal. block_a_done counts a released judge launch over the plan's units only when the valid record names its judge; block_complete for every other block wants each released judge launch named by the valid record. record-block-a-not-run may name a released judge launch with no record, also after block A's seal (a decision naming only judge launches). seal.py status prints one line per record (tags, exits, answers judged, hashes) and 'valid' or 'INVALID: reason'.

open_points: Block B's required set (R3, read from the kit; no block-B plan is recorded yet): the 24 arm/a0_arm runs at 1105-1107 (plan A; 18 under plan B), plus each B10 unit of block B's ref_eval (SP and scaling points) and safe_lora (default, conditional, certify per seed) jobs, from record-done's units list; no pinned re-judged unit. Not included: ref_train (recipe G and B+Qi reference trainings, engine run-one units that the judge route would also enumerate under --run-root); if they must be judged, add 'ref_train' to stage1_rules.JUDGED_RUN_KINDS (the lead's decision, not invented here). If block B's comparisons re-judge any earlier unit (for example a0 1101-1104 or block A units for one device per contrast), its pins must be added to REJUDGED_PINS['B'] - they do not exist yet.
Block B has no not-run route for a judge launch (record-block-a-not-run is block A's only): a failed block-B Granite would leave block B incomplete with no kit route.

One judge-completion record per block and one tag per judge: a judge split over two launches (HarmBench above about 94 units hits the 6 h cap) or a re-launch after the record is recorded has no route (a resume before recording works: record the final tag).
R3's seal-level record check repeats block_complete's (R2) by design; mutant B15-x-judge-files-unsealed is killed only by a test that bypasses block_complete.

R3 allows judge files of units outside the required set or of a judge the record does not name (counted as other_files), following R3's wording; refusing them is a one-line change if the lead prefers.

record-judges reads tmp/judge-pod/TAG/judge-pod-result.json and fetched/out/run-record.json at record time (by key; never printed): those folders must still exist then (the operator rule keeps them). This is stricter than R2's text.

It is not a stage-1 output and runbook step 3 already prints it; unchanged here (it is Gate B's print).
